verdict: Invesco's revenue rose 14% to $1.87B — mostly because QQQ's conversion to an ETF structure moved its fees onto Invesco's books — and operating income jumped 61%, though shareholder profit slipped 2% to $295M.

segments.name: Investment management fees
segments.note: Fees for managing funds and ETFs — up 28%, mostly because QQQ's conversion in late 2025 put its management fees on Invesco's income statement.

segments.name: Service & distribution fees
segments.note: Fees for servicing and distributing funds — down 22% because QQQ's conversion eliminated its pass-through service revenues.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Real-estate transaction fees and miscellaneous income.

segments.name: Performance fees
segments.note: Fees earned only when funds beat their targets — small this quarter.

opex.name: Employee compensation
opex.note: Pay and bonuses for portfolio managers and staff — an asset manager's biggest cost.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: The back office and professional services.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Promoting funds and ETFs, including QQQ.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions over time.

otherDetail: Earnings from unconsolidated affiliates of $43M, $30M of income from consolidated investment products and $10M of interest and dividend income, less $20M of interest expense and $34M of other investment losses — a net gain of about $28M.

takeaways.title: Look at 'net revenues' instead
takeaways.text: About $0.49B of GAAP revenue passes straight through to third parties. Invesco's own yardstick, net revenues, was $1.38B, up 16.5%, and its adjusted operating margin on that was 40.7%.

takeaways.title: Operating leverage showed up
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income jumped 61% to $437M as the QQQ fee change lifted revenue while employee compensation actually fell 5%.

takeaways.title: Assets keep growing
takeaways.text: Assets under management reached $2.54 trillion, up 19% year over year, on market gains and inflows.

oneTimers: QQQ's conversion to an open-end fund ETF in Q4 2025 reshaped the revenue lines: management fees gained roughly $328M year over year while service and distribution fees lost about $88M of pass-through revenue. It is a presentation change more than new business.
footerNote: Net income of $356M is before $24M attributable to noncontrolling interests and $37M of preferred-share dividends; net income attributable to Invesco common shareholders was $295M, the basis for the $0.65 EPS. This page uses GAAP figures; Invesco headlines 'net revenues' of $1,382M and adjusted operating income of $562M.
